> **Synthetic demonstration only.** This notebook is adapted from Anna Cho's
> PSYC 8803 course analysis. No ADNI records, original participant-level plots,
> or original numerical results are distributed. Data generation and publication
> changes were prepared with AI assistance; see `docs/PROVENANCE.md`.

Missingness patterns do not test MCAR, and a missingness regression cannot verify
MAR or rule out MNAR. Feature screening and subsequent inference reuse the same
sample: estimates, intervals and p-values are exploratory, even after BH adjustment.
WMH-zero exclusion changes the analysis population and is not an MNAR sensitivity model.

```{r setup, include=TRUE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = TRUE, message = TRUE)

library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(mice)
library(broom)
library(knitr)
library(purrr)

# This public notebook only accepts the generated, explicitly labelled demo.
if (basename(params$data_path) != "synthetic_demo.csv") {
  stop("This public notebook is configured for synthetic_demo.csv only.")
}
df <- read_csv(params$data_path, show_col_types = FALSE)
required <- c("DATA_SOURCE", "TAU_SUVR", "WMH_volume_mm3", "AGE",
              "PTGENDER", "interval_months", "SUVR_GlobalSUVR",
              sprintf("PEP%03d", 1:69))
stopifnot(all(required %in% names(df)), nrow(df) > 0,
          all(!is.na(df$DATA_SOURCE)),
          all(df$DATA_SOURCE == "SYNTHETIC_NOT_ADNI"))
df$DATA_SOURCE <- NULL
cat("SYNTHETIC DEMONSTRATION — not ADNI results. Rows:", nrow(df), "\n")
```

# 1. Missing Value Restoration

- Convert PTGENDER to a factor.
- Recode TAU_SUVR == 0 to missing (NA) for analysis.
- Keep WMH = 0 as observed in the main analysis; handle WMH zeros later in a sensitivity check.

```{r restore_missing}
df <- df %>%
  mutate(
    PTGENDER = factor(PTGENDER)
  )

df <- df %>%
  mutate(
    TAU_SUVR = ifelse(TAU_SUVR == 0, NA_real_, TAU_SUVR)
  )

cat("TAU missing:", sum(is.na(df$TAU_SUVR)), "\n")
cat("WMH missing:", sum(is.na(df$WMH_volume_mm3)), "\n")
cat("AGE missing:", sum(is.na(df$AGE)), "\n")
cat("interval missing:", sum(is.na(df$interval_months)), "\n")
cat("Rows:", nrow(df), "\n")
```

# 2. Missingness Summary

- Compute the proportion of missing values for all variables.
- Display the top 20 variables with the highest missingness.
- Visualize missingness for TAU_SUVR, WMH_volume_mm3, AGE, interval_months, SUVR_GlobalSUVR

```{r missing_summary}
missing_prop <- colMeans(is.na(df))
missing_prop_sorted <- sort(missing_prop, decreasing = TRUE)

kable(head(missing_prop_sorted, 20),
      caption = "Top 20 variables by missingness")

missing_matrix <- is.na(df[, c("TAU_SUVR", "WMH_volume_mm3", "AGE",
                               "interval_months", "SUVR_GlobalSUVR")])
image(seq_len(ncol(missing_matrix)), seq_len(nrow(missing_matrix)),
      t(missing_matrix * 1), col = c("grey90", "steelblue"),
      axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "Synthetic row", main = "Missingness (blue = missing)")
axis(1, at = seq_len(ncol(missing_matrix)), labels = colnames(missing_matrix), cex.axis = 0.6)
axis(2)
```

# 3. Descriptive Missingness Patterns

- Create a reduced dataset with TAU_SUVR, WMH_volume_mm3, AGE, PTGENDER, SUVR_GlobalSUVR.
- Use md.pattern to summarize joint missingness patterns.

```{r mcar_test}
df_mcar <- df %>%
  select(TAU_SUVR, WMH_volume_mm3, AGE, PTGENDER, SUVR_GlobalSUVR)

md.pattern(df_mcar, rotate.names = TRUE)
```

# 4. Associations with TAU Missingness

- Create a binary indicator TAU_missing (1 = TAU_SUVR missing, 0 = observed).
- Fit a logistic regression: TAU_missing ~ AGE + PTGENDER + SUVR_GlobalSUVR + WMH_volume_mm3.
- Report odds ratios for predictors of TAU missingness.

```{r miss_model}
df <- df %>% mutate(TAU_missing = ifelse(is.na(TAU_SUVR), 1, 0))

fit_logit <- glm(
  TAU_missing ~ AGE + PTGENDER + SUVR_GlobalSUVR + WMH_volume_mm3,
  data = df,
  family = binomial()
)

tidy(fit_logit, exponentiate = TRUE, conf.int = TRUE) %>%
  kable(digits = 3,
        caption = "Predictors of TAU missingness (OR scale)")
```

- Compare observed vs missing TAU groups on age, sex, amyloid SUVR, WMH.

```{r complete_vs_incomplete}
df %>%
  group_by(TAU_missing) %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    mean_age = mean(AGE, na.rm = TRUE),
    prop_female = mean(PTGENDER == "Female", na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_global_suvr = mean(SUVR_GlobalSUVR, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_WMH = mean(WMH_volume_mm3, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) %>%
  kable(digits = 2,
        caption = "Complete vs incomplete cases (by TAU availability)")
```

# 5. Peptide screening

- Identify 69 explicitly named synthetic peptide-like variables (PEP001–PEP069).
- Define a screening subset (df_cc_screen) with complete data on TAU_SUVR, AGE, PTGENDER, interval_months.
- For each peptide, fit: TAU_SUVR ~ peptide + AGE + PTGENDER + interval_months.
- Extract peptide coefficients and p-values, then rank peptides by p-value.
- Select the smallest-p-value feature for an exploratory demonstration; it is not a prespecified confirmatory test.
- Plot TAU_SUVR vs selected peptide with a fitted regression line for the complete cases.

```{r Peptide_screening}
peptide_vars <- sprintf("PEP%03d", 1:69)

length(peptide_vars)  # 69

# Subset of TAU + covariates complete case for screening
df_cc_screen <- df %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(TAU_SUVR),
    !is.na(AGE),
    !is.na(PTGENDER),
    !is.na(interval_months)
  )
nrow(df_cc_screen)

screen_results <- map_dfr(peptide_vars, ~{
    form <- as.formula(
      paste("TAU_SUVR ~", .x, "+ AGE + PTGENDER + interval_months"))
    fit <- lm(form, data = df_cc_screen)
    
    broom::tidy(fit) %>%
      dplyr::filter(term == .x) %>%
      mutate(peptide = .x)
  }
)

screen_table <- screen_results %>%
  mutate(p.adjusted.BH = p.adjust(p.value, method = "BH")) %>%
  arrange(p.value) %>%
  select(peptide, estimate, std.error, statistic, p.value, p.adjusted.BH)

screen_table %>%
  head(10) %>%
  kable(digits = 8,
        caption = "Top 10 peptides associated with TAU SUVR (complete cases)")

peptide_var <- screen_table %>%
  slice(1) %>%
  pull(peptide)

peptide_var  # Determined from synthetic data; not the original study selection.

df_cc_plot <- df_cc_screen %>%
  filter(!is.na(.data[[peptide_var]]))

ggplot(df_cc_plot, aes(x = .data[[peptide_var]], y = TAU_SUVR)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE) +
  labs(
    x = paste("CSF peptide (", peptide_var, ")", sep = ""),
    y = "TAU SUVR",
    title = "Association between peptide and TAU SUVR (complete cases)"
  )
```

# 6. Complete-Case Regression

- Construct a complete-case dataset (df_cc) requiring observed TAU_SUVR, selected peptide, AGE, PTGENDER, interval_months.
- Fit the linear regression: TAU_SUVR ~ selected_feature + AGE + PTGENDER + interval_months.

```{r complete_case}
df_cc <- df %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(TAU_SUVR),
    !is.na(.data[[peptide_var]]),
    !is.na(AGE),
    !is.na(PTGENDER),
    !is.na(interval_months)
  )

form_cc <- as.formula(
  paste("TAU_SUVR ~", peptide_var, "+ AGE + PTGENDER + interval_months")
)

fit_cc <- lm(form_cc, data = df_cc)

tidy(fit_cc) %>%
  kable(digits = 4,
        caption = paste("Complete-case regression for", peptide_var))
```

# 7. Multiple Imputation under MAR

- Restrict the imputation sample to participants with non-missing WMH_volume_mm3.
- Select variables for imputation: TAU_SUVR, AGE, PTGENDER, interval_months, WMH_volume_mm3, SUVR_GlobalSUVR, and selected peptide.
- Use PMM for incomplete numeric variables and logistic regression for incomplete binary PTGENDER; skip fully observed columns.
- Set the predictor-matrix diagonal to zero. Any missing auxiliary variable is also imputed.
- Generate 20 imputations by default. This assumes MAR conditional on the included predictors; it does not establish MAR.

```{r mi_setup}
df_mi <- df %>%
  filter(!is.na(WMH_volume_mm3)) %>%
  select(
    TAU_SUVR,
    AGE,
    PTGENDER,
    interval_months,
    WMH_volume_mm3,
    SUVR_GlobalSUVR,
    all_of(peptide_var)
  )
colnames(df_mi)

# A matched complete-case model separates population restriction from imputation.
fit_cc_matched <- lm(form_cc, data = df_mi, na.action = na.omit)
make_spec <- function(data) {
  ini <- mice(data, maxit = 0, printFlag = FALSE)
  method <- ini$method
  for (name in names(data)) {
    method[name] <- if (!anyNA(data[[name]])) "" else if (is.factor(data[[name]])) "logreg" else "pmm"
  }
  pred <- ini$predictorMatrix
  diag(pred) <- 0
  list(method = method, predictor = pred)
}
spec <- make_spec(df_mi)

imp <- mice(
  df_mi,
  m = params$imputations, maxit = params$iterations,
  method = spec$method,
  predictorMatrix = spec$predictor,
  seed = 123, printFlag = FALSE
)
imp
plot(imp)  # Inspect chain traces; this is a diagnostic, not a guarantee.
imp$loggedEvents
```

# 8. Pooled Regression after MI

- In each imputed dataset, fit the same regression model as the complete-case analysis.
- Pool estimates across imputations using Rubin’s rules.
- Extract pooled estimates, standard errors, confidence intervals, RIV, and FMI.
- Compare the selected peptide effect between complete-case and MI analyses.

```{r mi_pool}
nrow(df_mi)

fit_mi <- with(
  imp,
  lm(
    as.formula(
      paste("TAU_SUVR ~", peptide_var, "+ AGE + PTGENDER + interval_months")
    )
  )
)

pool_mi <- pool(fit_mi)

mi_basic <- summary(pool_mi, conf.int = TRUE, conf.level = 0.95)

mi_extra <- pool_mi$pooled %>%
  dplyr::select(term, riv, lambda, fmi) %>%
  dplyr::rename(
    RIV    = riv,
    Lambda = lambda,
    FMI    = fmi
  )

mi_summary <- mi_basic %>%
  dplyr::left_join(mi_extra, by = "term")

mi_summary %>%
  kable(
    digits = 4,
    caption = "Pooled MI regression"
  )
```

```{r comparison_selected_peptide}
compare_est <- data.frame(
method = c("Complete-case (all eligible)", "Complete-case (MI population)", "MI (MAR)"),
estimate = c(
fit_cc$coefficients[peptide_var],
fit_cc_matched$coefficients[peptide_var],
mi_summary$estimate[mi_summary$term == peptide_var])
)

ggplot(compare_est, aes(x = method, y = estimate)) +
geom_point(size = 4) +
geom_segment(aes(x = method, xend = method,
y = 0, yend = estimate),
alpha = 0.4) +
theme_minimal() +
labs(
y = "Estimated effect on TAU SUVR",
x = "",
title = "Comparison of selected peptide Effect: Complete Case vs MI")
```

# 9. WMH = 0 Sensitivity Scenario

- Scenario A: Use the MI results where WMH = 0 is kept as a valid value (mi_A).
- Scenario B: Recode WMH_volume_mm3 = 0 as NA, restrict to non-missing WMH, and re-run MI (mi_B).
- Fit the same pooled regression model in Scenario B.
- Compare the selected peptide estimates and standard errors between Scenario A and B.

```{r wmh_sensitivity}
## Scenario A: main MI (WMH = 0 kept as 0)
mi_A <- mi_summary %>%
  mutate(scenario = "WMH: 0 kept as 0")

## Scenario B: treat WMH = 0 as missing
df_wmh_na <- df %>%
  mutate(WMH_volume_mm3 = ifelse(WMH_volume_mm3 == 0, NA, WMH_volume_mm3))

sum(is.na(df_wmh_na$WMH_volume_mm3))

df_mi_B <- df_wmh_na %>%
  filter(!is.na(WMH_volume_mm3)) %>%
  select(
    TAU_SUVR,
    AGE,
    PTGENDER,
    interval_months,
    WMH_volume_mm3,
    SUVR_GlobalSUVR,
    all_of(peptide_var)
  )

spec_B <- make_spec(df_mi_B)

set.seed(456)
imp_B <- mice(
  df_mi_B,
  m = params$imputations, maxit = params$iterations,
  method = spec_B$method,
  predictorMatrix = spec_B$predictor, printFlag = FALSE
)

fit_mi_B <- with(
  imp_B,
  lm(
    as.formula(
      paste("TAU_SUVR ~", peptide_var, "+ AGE + PTGENDER + interval_months")
    )
  )
)

pool_mi_B <- pool(fit_mi_B)

mi_B <- summary(pool_mi_B, conf.int = TRUE, conf.level = 0.95) %>%
  mutate(scenario = "WMH: 0 treated as NA")

sens_wmh <- bind_rows(mi_A, mi_B) %>%
  filter(term == peptide_var) %>%
  select(
    scenario, estimate, std.error, statistic, df, p.value,
    `2.5 %`, `97.5 %`
  )

sens_wmh %>%
  kable(
    digits  = 4,
    caption = "Sensitivity of peptide effect to WMH=0 handling (0 vs NA)",
    row.names = FALSE
  )
```

# 10. Optional: Bayesian complete case regression

- Fit a Bayesian version of the complete-case regression model using brms: TAU_SUVR ~ selected_feature + AGE + PTGENDER + interval_months.
- Use priors: b ~ Normal(0, 5), sigma ~ Student_t(3, 0, 10).
- Run 4 chains with 4000 iterations each (1000 warmup), check convergence (Rhat, ESS).
- Summarize posterior means and 95% credible intervals for all coefficients.

```{r bayes_cc, eval=FALSE}
library(brms)
library(rstan)
options(mc.cores = parallel::detectCores())
rstan::rstan_options(auto_write = TRUE)

brm_cc <- brm(
  formula = form_cc,
  data    = df_cc,
  family  = gaussian(),
  prior   = c(
    set_prior("normal(0, 5)", class = "b"),
    set_prior("student_t(3, 0, 10)", class = "sigma")
  ),
  seed    = 2025,
  chains  = 4,
  iter    = 4000,
  warmup  = 1000
)

summary(brm_cc)
```

# Interpretation limits

Synthetic outputs illustrate the workflow only. They do not reproduce the ADNI
study or support clinical conclusions. Inspect imputation warnings, logged events,
and chain traces before interpreting any estimates. The optional Bayesian block
is disabled by default and requires a separate brms/Stan installation.
